Why 1584×396

LinkedIn personal profile banners are 1584×396 — an unusually wide 4:1 strip, which is why ordinary photos look badly cropped up there.

The image is centre-cropped to the target shape and then scaled, which is what keeps proportions correct — squeezing a whole photo into a different aspect ratio is what makes faces look stretched. The page reports roughly how much was trimmed, and the full resizer lets you control the crop yourself.
LinkedIn overlays your profile photo on the lower-left of the banner and crops the edges on narrow screens. Keep anything important in the middle third.
No. The work happens in this tab using Canvas. Your image never touches a server, which is also why it keeps working with no network once the page has loaded.
